reviews.text: It's really goood. I like this game. There are 8 different characters, each with their own unique abilities. The gameplay felt great as I progressed through the game trying out the characters. The difficulty level also increases nicely. A successful roguelike game is on the horizon.

It turned out to be more enjoyable than I expected. The gameplay is smooth, and the battles are quite satisfying. I just wanted to jump in and take a quick look, but I ended up playing for a long time :)

I've got around 7 hours in so far, and it's been a pleasant surprise. I usually get bored pretty quickly if a roguelike doesn't have satisfying combat, but this one kept pulling me back for "just one more run." The different characters actually feel distinct instead of being simple stat changes, and trying out new builds has been the most enjoyable part for me. Some runs are brutal, but when everything finally clicks together it feels really rewarding. It's still in early access, so there are rough edges here and there, but the core gameplay is solid and that's what matters most. If the developers keep adding content and polishing what's already here, I can easily see myself putting a lot more hours into it. Definitely worth keeping an eye on. Looking forward to future updates.

It's a pretty well made roguelike game, with sufficiently diverse, interesting characters, which bring about many playing styles and different builds, and the game offers a lot of replayability. Visuals are pretty slick too, with cool lighting and animations. Well worth a buy.

The game seems really promising. The pixel art style is really cute and looks great. The multiplayer option is a valuable addition to the genre. At the moment, melee and ranged characters don't feel completely balanced. Currently melee characters is being punished more than ranged ones. I also think the weapon system could benefit from having more unique weapons instead of the typical hack-and-slash style loot drops. But ofc it a design decision. The game's atmosphere is really enjoyable, and with more content and polish in future updates, I'm sure it will become an even better experience.

Wartheon is a roguelike game in which we have to clear dungeons from various enemies and bosses. However, the design of the locations and the leveling system are at a low level. There are also bugs.
Large scale battles reward smart positioning instead of blind aggression, while the fantasy setting and varied unit roster keep each encounter feeling fresh.

While there is potential here, this game has not been polished nearly enough to be released on Steam.
